method.basis: Current OpenAPI contract, current frontend owner/adapter code, direct tests, and the auth MFA/session specification. Current dirty worktree files are identified by SHA-256 below; HEAD alone does not represent them.
method.interpretation: Contract declaration, frontend implementation, test simulation, and backend runtime proof are separate evidence classes. A test using MSW proves frontend behavior only. Missing or ambiguous backend semantics remain unknown.

focusedTestRun.command: node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --reporter=dot src/app/contexts/AuthSessionProvider.test.tsx src/shared/session/auth-context.test.ts src/features/auth/api/auth-api.test.ts src/features/trading/api/trading-api.test.ts src/features/wallet/api/wallet-api.test.ts src/features/p2p/api/p2p-api.test.ts src/features/dca/api/dca-api.test.ts
focusedTestRun.environment: Windows 11 Pro; Node.js v24.19.0; Vitest 4.1.11; local test adapters/MSW; no backend or staging connection

observed: POST /auth/login returns authenticated or mfa_required; the provider only applies a session for authenticated. Login MFA verification returns a session only after a successful challenge verification.

The auth spec says the challenge must belong to that login, be unexpired and unused. Contract responses include invalid 400, expired 410, locked 423 and rate-limited 429; exact duplicate-verification response is not declared.

AuthContext uses an operation serial. Local logout clears session/token before I/O and increments the serial; stale auth results cannot overwrite a newer local state. Provider tests cover late refresh/bootstrap/login/MFA results and cross-tab logout races.
Session revocation is described by the API as logout 204, but frontend tests do not prove server-side cookie/token invalidation.

invariants.rule: Do not create authenticated frontend state from the mfa_required login branch; apply session only after a verified response.
An obsolete in-flight auth operation must not restore session, token, or error after a newer auth operation/logout.
Backend challenge single-use, expiry, rate limit, lockout, and actual session revocation must hold server-side.

gaps: Login/MFA requests have no Idempotency-Key rule; duplicate login/challenge issuance semantics are unspecified.
Near-concurrent requests are serialized only for local provider state; backend session issuance/revocation ordering is not established.
A client timeout or lost response after login/logout/refresh cannot establish whether the server changed its cookie/session.

observed: placeOrder requires an idempotency key and declares 201, 400 and 409 (duplicate key or insufficient balance). modifyOrder/cancelOrder require keys and declare success plus 404; their conflict/replay rules are not declared.

Order snapshots require amount > 0, filled >= 0, filled <= amount; filled status requires full fill and partial status requires a nonzero fill below amount. The status enum is open/filled/partial/cancelled/rejected.

Adapter methods send mutations with retries: 0 and validate returned order shape. API tests cover the key and response parsing. One cancel test simulates 409 ORDER_ALREADY_CLOSED although the current cancel OpenAPI response list has no 409; this is a test/contract mismatch, not a confirmed backend behavior.

invariants.rule: Reject malformed order snapshots and inconsistent fill/status combinations at the adapter boundary.
Place-order request must include a key; create conflict/duplicate is represented as 409 by contract.
Modify/cancel only legal from server-approved order states; stale concurrent writes must not reverse terminal state.

gaps: No exact key scope, replay result, payload-conflict policy, retention period, or reconciliation query is declared.
Allowed source states and outcomes for modify/cancel, out-of-order actions and near-concurrent fill/cancel are unspecified.
The cancel 409 test fixture is not listed in current OpenAPI; reconcile contract vs test before treating it as supported.
Timeout after an order may have been accepted has no operation lookup/reconciliation contract in this path.

observed: Transfers require wallet:transfer and a key of at least 16 characters; 201 is accepted, 409 combines duplicate key/conflicting transfer. Withdrawals similarly declare 201 and 409 for duplicate request/insufficient funds.

Withdrawal challenge issuance returns a one-time challenge; verification returns a short-lived authorization token and 401 for invalid/expired code. The OpenAPI explicitly leaves issuance replay and one-time verification replay semantics undefined.
Adapter sends transfer/withdrawal/challenge mutations with retries: 0. Direct tests prove configured headers and response parsing only; they do not prove backend replay or persistence.

invariants.rule: Do not treat transfer/withdrawal as successful without a validated receipt; the same business request carries a required idempotency key.
Withdrawal sequence is challenge issuance -> verification token -> withdrawal submission; verification failure must not authorize submit.
Resolve a timeout/lost response or duplicate safely before allowing the user to repeat a money movement.

gaps: The user confirmed the Wallet unknown/duplicate backend contract is not available. A generic 409 declaration is insufficient to resolve an unknown-after-I/O outcome.
No lookup/correlation operation for a receipt-less transfer/withdrawal, authoritative replay response, same-key payload mismatch rule, or backend retention window is identified.
Challenge issue/verify duplicate and concurrent consumption semantics are explicitly not specified; do not auto-retry them.

observed: Create-order uses Idempotency-Key and declares 201/409. mark-paid and escrow release use keys, return an order on 200 and declare 409 when the order cannot transition to paid/released.

Order status values are pending_payment/paid/released/disputed/cancelled/expired. The enum is not a full allowed-transition table; it does not specify actor/state preconditions for each endpoint beyond broad 409.

Release challenge issuance and verification are one-time challenge flow exceptions with replay semantics explicitly unspecified. The permission annotations for create/pay/release remain draft_frontend with unresolved backend ownership and enforcement questions.

invariants.rule: A successful paid/released status comes from the validated server response; only a transition accepted by server is reflected.
Invalid paid/release transition returns 409 as declared; caller/actor/resource authorization is enforced by backend.
Concurrent paid/release or timeout/replay must not release escrow more than once or falsely report success.

gaps: Exact allowed from/to states, buyer/seller/merchant ownership, atomic transition and concurrency winner are not fully declared.
Idempotency behavior for mark-paid/release (same-key replay, conflicting payload and retention) is not defined; the transition 409 is not a replay protocol.
Release challenge/verify replay is unspecified; permission scopes are draft_frontend, not evidence of server authorization.
Unknown-after-I/O has no authoritative reconciliation path evidenced here.

observed: create/update/delete require Idempotency-Key; create returns 201, update 200, delete 204, and update/delete declare 404 for a missing plan. Plan status values are active/paused/error; amountPerPurchase must be positive.
DCA query mutations invalidate the snapshot on successful writes. API methods explicitly use retries: 0; tests assert a key is sent and a fixture response is parsed.
The OpenAPI does not declare duplicate/conflict status, version/If-Match precondition, status transition matrix, or concurrency/replay policy.

invariants.rule: Accept only schema-valid plan snapshots and positive purchase amounts; re-read the server snapshot after successful mutation.
A stale update/delete must not silently overwrite a newer plan or purchase schedule.
Resolve duplicate or unknown-after-I/O plan mutations before reporting definitive state.

gaps: Idempotency-Key presence is not a replay guarantee; duplicate status/response and retention are undefined.
No concurrency version/precondition or exact allowed state transition is declared.
A timed-out plan mutation can have committed; no mutation receipt lookup is evident from this operation contract.

crossCuttingCases.finding: Auth MFA gate, trading request/snapshot schemas, wallet receipt/challenge types, P2P response schemas and DCA plan schemas are visible in contracts/adapters. This establishes client boundaries, not server enforcement.
Auth and P2P declare selected rejection codes; place-order declares 400; wallet declares selected 401/403/409; DCA has 404 only for missing plans. No full backend guard matrix exists.

Keys are required for several mutations; duplicate behavior is explicit only for selected create paths. Key lifecycle, payload conflict, exact replay result and retention are missing; Wallet unknown/duplicate lookup remains a user-confirmed blocker.
Auth MFA sequence and broad P2P impossible-transition 409 are described. Trading modify/cancel, Wallet challenge replay, and DCA status transitions lack complete transition contracts.
Auth provider serial prevents stale local state writes and its race tests pass. Backend atomicity/order for trading, wallet, P2P escrow and DCA is not declared or tested against a real server.
Shared HTTP client deadline defaults to 15,000 ms; mutation adapters use retries: 0. A timeout/abort after request dispatch does not prove the server did not commit.

No general operation-status/correlation recovery flow is established for receipt-less writes. Do not tell users a money/order mutation failed or auto-resubmit solely from timeout; require an approved backend lookup/replay contract.

blockers.owner: backend contract owner not identified in this frontend checkout
blockers.detail: User confirmed no approved Wallet unknown/duplicate contract is available. Define authoritative lookup/correlation, replay, conflicting-payload and recovery behavior before certifying transfer/withdrawal handling.
P2P permission annotations are draft_frontend; define server-side actor/ownership/state guards, atomic near-concurrent transitions and replay behavior.
Trading/P2P/DCA (and auth session writes) lack sufficient operation reconciliation semantics after timeout/lost response.

trading-api.test.ts simulates cancelOrder 409 ORDER_ALREADY_CLOSED while contracts/openapi/trading.yaml currently omits 409 for cancelOrder. Reconcile the declared contract or the test fixture before relying on this outcome.
